name: Wordwall
tagline: Turns a teacher's word list into interactive classroom games and printable worksheets from a library of templates.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core trick is genuinely simple: you type a list of pairs or questions once, then the same data renders as a quiz, a match-up, a wordsearch, a spinning wheel, an anagram. An agent can ship six or eight of those templates in a sitting, driven off one JSON file, and for a teacher who reuses the same four activity types that is most of the product. What you will not one-shot is the full template count, the animation polish that keeps eight-year-olds engaged, the printable worksheet variants, and the enormous library of activities other teachers already made and shared. If you mostly search that library instead of authoring, this is not a build, it is a subscription. If you author your own content, the DIY version is a real option.
coreLoopDIY: One local web app where you enter a list of question/answer or word/definition pairs and instantly play or print that same list as any of several game templates.
requirements: A place to host the static build if you want it on a classroom projector or shared tablet
Your own content: no shared activity library comes with it
whatYouLose: The community library of millions of ready-made activities, which is the reason many people subscribe at all
Template breadth: the real thing has dozens, your build will have a handful
Kid-grade animation, sound and mobile touch polish that took years to tune
Printable worksheet output that actually looks like a worksheet
Sharing links, class assignment tracking and result leaderboards
moatNotes: The template engine is copyable. The pile of teacher-made activities sitting on top of it, and the search that finds them, is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Teachers are not short on ideas, they are short on prep minutes at 10pm. Paying means typing a topic into a search box and finding forty activities someone already built, then reskinning one into a wheel and projecting it. A self-hosted clone gives you the engine but hands the content authoring back to you, which is exactly the labour the subscription was buying out. It also just works on the school iPad, which matters more than any feature list.
notes: Build it if you write your own content, subscribe if you shop for other people's.
prompt:
Build a local-first classroom activity generator as a static web app. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript, plain CSS (no UI framework), Zustand or React context for state. Persist everything to localStorage. Include an export/import of the full library as a single JSON file so activities can be moved between machines.

Data model: an Activity has an id, title, subject tag, and a list of items. Each item is { term, match } plus optional { options: string[], correct: number } for multiple choice. One activity's item list must be renderable by every template, so validate that terms and matches are non-empty and warn when an item lacks options for choice-based templates.

Editor: a single spreadsheet-style grid to type or paste items (accept tab-separated paste from Excel or Google Sheets), plus a title field and a template picker. Autosave on change.

Implement exactly these six templates, each a full-screen play view driven off the same item list:
1. Quiz: one question at a time, four choices, score and timer.
2. Match Up: drag terms onto matches, snap on correct, shake on wrong.
3. Wordsearch: generate a grid from the terms, click-drag to select, list of words to find.
4. Spin the Wheel: SVG wheel of terms, weighted-random spin with easing, removes or keeps entries via a toggle.
5. Flashcards: click to flip term to match, arrow keys to advance, shuffle button.
6. Anagram: scrambled letters of each term, drag or type to unscramble, hint reveals first letter.

All play views must work with mouse, touch and keyboard, and must look correct projected at 1920x1080. Big type, high contrast, no hover-only affordances.

Also add a Print view: renders the current activity as a printable worksheet using @media print, one for wordsearch grids and one generic term/match table with blank lines. Browser print to PDF is the only export.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, sharing links, a public activity library, class rosters, score history across sessions, sound effects, leaderboards.

Ship with three seed activities so the app is not empty on first load, a README with run instructions, and no .env (there are no secrets).
